# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 62 (Bu-Vb Pc62)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc62
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 62
**Title (English, from literature):** Using water with living beings in it
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sappāṇaka Sutta* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 62) sets out the monastic training rule forbidding a Buddhist monk from knowingly using water containing living beings, an infraction that entails an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*). In modern scholarship, Lambert Schmithausen notes that Pācittiya 62, alongside Pācittiya 20 (which prohibits sprinkling water containing tiny creatures), functions as a borderline application of the general ethical prohibition against killing animals (enunciated in Pācittiya 61) [Schmithausen 1991; Hüsken 1997]. In her comparative study of the Sarvāstivāda Vinayavibhaṅga, Valentina Rosen examines the casuistry of Pācittiya 62 in conjunction with its Sarvāstivādin counterpart, Pātayantika 41, analyzing how the legal analysis treats permutations of the monk's awareness and the actual presence of living organisms in the water [Rosen 1959].

 Direct counterparts include rule 41 of the Sarvāstivāda and Mūlasarvāstivāda Bhikṣuvibhaṅgas (extant in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit fragments), rule 51 in the Mahāsāṅghika tradition, rule 62 in the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya, as well as parallel regulations in the respective Bhikṣuṇī vibhaṅgas (such as Pali Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 143). DharmaNexus computational analysis highlights significant Pali-internal textual reuse, most prominently with Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 20 (sharing segments §1.4–2.1.7 with §1.5–2.1.6), Pācittiya 63, and Pācittiya 76, as well as alignment with Tibetan Vinaya exegetical literature, specifically the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkā Vinayasamuccaya* (D4106) [DharmaNexus].
